title: Goose index entry
description: One hand-written file, packages/<id>.toml. Facts that change on their own (tags, stars, dates, archived, detected license) are not written here: scripts/fetch_meta.py fetches them into data/meta.json. See schema/README.md.

id.description: Equals the file name without .toml. Lowercase owner and repository joined by '-', e.g. kaitk-goose-sqlite. Never changes once published, since index.json consumers key on it.

name.description: Display name, usually the repository name.

kind.description: package: a Goose library imported with `import x from "..."`. binding: a Goose library whose work is done by a library in another language (C, Rust...). tool: a program for Goose developers. editor: editor or IDE support. app: a program written in Goose. fork: a fork or derivative of the Goose compiler. learning-resource: tutorials, guides, articles, examples, benchmarks.

category.description: Exactly one; see schema/categories.toml for each one's title and scope.

tags.description: Lowercase search keywords, most specific first.

repo.description: The git repository, as an https URL without .git. Required unless kind is learning-resource and url is given.

url.description: For a learning-resource that is not a repository (an article, a video): its address.

description.description: One or two sentences in the index's own words, never copied from the project's README or GitHub description. scripts/validate.py rejects six or more words in a row shared with the project's own description.

import.description: Required for package and binding. The index builds the import line from it and the latest tag in data/meta.json: import <name> from "<path>@<tag>";

name.description: The name the package is imported as (its root namespace).

path.description: Only when it differs from the repository: what goes before @ in the import string.

subdir.description: The package's folder inside the repository, when it is not the root. Goose cannot fetch such a package by URL yet (upstream docs/design/packages.md §11), so the site shows how to copy the folder instead of an import line.

modules.description: Further modules users import by name after declaring the package, e.g. net.http.

native.description: What building it needs besides Goose, so CI can install it. c and cmake come from the project's .build sidecars.

c.description: Compiles C sources (c_sources in a sidecar).

cmake.description: Builds a CMake project (cmake_target in a sidecar).

system_libs.description: Packages a machine must have installed, named as that platform's package manager names them: apt (Debian/Ubuntu) for linux, Homebrew for macos, vcpkg or a short note for windows.

tools.description: Other programs the build runs (python3, cargo...).

platforms.description: Platforms the author says it supports. Empty when the author does not say.

license_override.description: Only when GitHub's license detection is wrong or missing but the project does state a license: its SPDX id.

upstream_fork.description: For kind fork: what the fork adds, in a few words, shown on its page.

compat.description: For the compatibility runner. skip: never build it (an app needing hardware, a fork). entry: the file to check, when it is not <import.name>.goose at the root.
